messages.author: 139f4e1532ac2d5f
messages.subject: andRule and orRule simsem
parts:
I run a Monte Carlo simulation for model evaluation (simsem).

From the help page:
"The p values of fit indices are provided, as well as two additional values: andRule and orRule. The andRule is based on the principle that the model is retained only when all fit indices provide good fit. [...]. The orRule is based on the principle that the model is retained only when at least one fit index provides good fit. [...]. The proportion from the orRule is the most lenient rule in retaining a hypothesized model."

My p values:
 andRule   0.0000000
orRule 0.2911917

Does it make sense? andRule is telling me that all fit indices provide good fit as it is significant, the orRule is telling me that the hypothesis that at least one fit index provides good fit could not be accepted. I think I am misunderstanding the meaning of the andRule and orRule. If the hypothesis of the andRule as true is accepted, why is the one of orRule not? (which should be more "lenient"). I can see a possible case when orRule is accepted and the andRule is not, but not the other way. Could you help me interpret this?

The complete output:
chisq       0.0000000
aic           0.2911917
bic           0.2911917
rmsea      0.0000000
 cfi            0.0000000
 tli              0.0000000
 srmr          0.0000000
andRule    0.0000000
orRule       0.2911917

Thanks!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: andRule and orRule simsem
parts:
Does it make sense?

Yes, the or-rule is more lenient, so it retains more models.  29% of samples (p = .29) yielded worse information criteria than the model fitted to the actual data, so those don't reject the  H0 of good fit.  But for all other indices, the observed ones were worse than for all simulated data, so those p values are all ~0, reject the H0.
andRule is telling me that all fit indices provide good fit as it is significant

No, the H0 is good fit, and low p values lead to rejecting that H0.  Just like the standard chi-squared test of model fit.
